headline: Gemini for macOS adds iMessage integration, allowing send and read functions
summary: Google's latest update to the Gemini app for macOS readies local iMessage integration. This follows the app's recent launch on Windows, expanding its cross-platform utility.
details: Google's Gemini app for macOS is receiving an update that enables local iMessage integration. This new functionality will allow users to send and read iMessages directly within the Gemini application.
This macOS update follows the recent release of the Gemini app for Windows last week. The expansion to Apple's desktop operating system broadens Gemini's reach and utility across different platforms.
caption:
Google's Gemini app for macOS is getting a major update. You'll soon be able to send and read iMessages directly within the AI assistant.

Google's Gemini app for macOS is receiving an update that enables local iMessage integration. This new functionality will allow users to send and read iMessages directly within the Gemini application.

This macOS update follows the recent release of the Gemini app for Windows last week. The expansion to Apple's desktop operating system broadens Gemini's reach and utility across different platforms.

headline_marked: [[India mandates caller-ID apps share spam reports]] with telcos, Truecaller calls it 'anti-competitive'
headline: India mandates caller-ID apps share spam reports with telcos, Truecaller calls it 'anti-competitive'
summary: India's telecom regulator now requires apps like Truecaller to send user spam reports to a blockchain-based platform run by operators. Truecaller, with 350M+ users in India, labels this a "one-way exchange" and "anti-competitive."
details: India's Telecom Regulatory Authority (TRAI) has amended rules, mandating caller-ID and call-management apps to share user spam reports with telecom operators. This move has prompted Truecaller, a leading spam-blocking app, to criticize the ruling as anti-competitive.

The new requirement aims to broaden the pool of spam reports available for action against spammers, connecting app-collected data with the telecom industry's enforcement infrastructure. India faces an enormous scale of spam and fraudulent calls, with Truecaller users encountering around 42 billion spam calls in 2025.

Truecaller, which has over 350 million monthly active users in India, its largest market, uses community reports, automated detection, and other signals to identify and block spam calls. The company views this mandate as a "one-way exchange" that transfers commercially valuable data to telecom operators.

This isn't the first time Truecaller and the Indian regulator have clashed over spam call handling. Truecaller previously objected to restrictions preventing apps from automatically labeling calls from certain government-designated number ranges as spam.

The latest amendments retain that restriction, barring call-management apps from blanket blocking or spam-tagging calls from designated series used for promotional, service, and transactional communications. Individual users, however, can still choose to block such calls on their devices.

A Truecaller spokesperson stated that their data and user sentiment clearly indicate a significant increase in spam due to this "free pass" given to spammers. Despite their concerns, the company has been compliant with this specific restriction since late last year.

Experts note that this change bridges two distinct layers: telecom operators providing the network and anti-spam system, and caller-ID apps operating on top. This raises technical and jurisdictional questions regarding reporting standards and enforcement against non-telecom companies.

Key details remain unclear, including the exact amount of information apps must provide, how users will be notified or asked for consent, and how the data can be retained and used. TRAI has not responded to questions regarding these specifics or whether the rule applies to built-in smartphone spam features.

Additionally, the amendments address the increasing use of software and AI voice agents for calls. Automatically made calls, without direct human dialing, will now fall under TRAI's application-to-person (A2P) framework.
